THOUGHT: The patient has diffuse, bright-red, cobblestoned gingival enlargement with ulceration and a rubbery multinodular texture. Histology shows dense sheets of bland plasmacytoid (CD138+) cells but immunostaining for light chains demonstrates a polyclonal population (both κ and λ). A polyclonal plasma-cell–predominant infiltrate plus the classic clinical appearance strongly favors a reactive/inflammatory plasma cell lesion of the gingiva (plasma cell gingivitis / plasma cell mucositis). The timing after starting pembrolizumab raises the possibility that this is an immune‑related mucosal reaction (checkpoint inhibitor–associated plasmacytic mucositis) or that pembrolizumab unmasked or exacerbated a contact/allergic plasma cell gingivitis. Monoclonal plasma‑cell neoplasms (extramedullary plasmacytoma, plasmablastic lymphoma, oral involvement of multiple myeloma) can have similar morphology but would be expected to show light‑chain restriction (monoclonality) and/or cytologic atypia; those features are not present here, making them much less likely though still important to consider until clinico‑pathologic correlation and staging/exclusion of systemic disease are completed.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Plasma cell gingivitis / plasma cell mucositis (reactive inflammatory plasma‑cell proliferation of the gingiva) — most likely given clinical appearance and polyclonal CD138+ infiltrate.
2. Immune checkpoint inhibitor–associated plasmacytic mucositis (pembrolizumab‑related immune‑mediated oral mucosal reaction presenting as plasma cell–predominant gingivitis) — favored given temporal relationship to therapy.
3. Extramedullary plasmacytoma (solitary plasmacytoma of oral soft tissue) — less likely because immunohistochemistry shows polyclonality, but included because morphology can overlap and clinical correlation/ systemic workup is needed to exclude.
4. Plasma cell gingivitis secondary to chronic/local irritants or contact hypersensitivity (allergic/contact plasma cell gingivitis) — possible alternative reactive cause (flavorings, toothpaste, chewing gum, periodontal disease).
5. Plasmablastic lymphoma or other aggressive plasmacytoid lymphoma / oral lymphoma (including oral involvement by multiple myeloma) — least likely given bland cytology and polyclonality, but should be considered if clinical course, additional biopsies, or systemic studies suggest malignancy.

Case Information:
An elderly man with undifferentiated pleomorphic sarcoma enrolled in a clinical trial of neoadjuvant treatment with pembrolizumab and radiation therapy. Six months after starting pembrolizumab, he developed gum pain and bleeding.

Physical Examination:
The maxillary and mandibular buccal gingivae appeared diffusely enlarged, erythematous, and cobblestoned. In the right maxillary quadrant, the gingival erythema and enlargement involved the buccal and labial mucosa. Crateriform and fissured ulcerations were identified in the right maxillary buccal vestibule that extended onto the right superior aspect of the buccal mucosa. The lesional tissue had a multinodular appearance and was rubbery firm.

Diagnostic Tests:
- Histopathologic examination:    - Biopsy showed sheets of uniform CD138+ plasmacytoid cells with rare acute and chronic inflammatory cells    - Immunohistochemical studies using antibodies directed against κ and λ light chains confirmed a polyclonal plasma cell infiltrate      - Images:    Figure 1. Clinical Findings    Description: A. Diffuse enlargement, erythema, and cobblestoning of the maxillary and mandibular buccal gingivae. B. The ulcerated hyperplastic tissue in these areas was rubbery firm on palpation.        Figure 2. Histopathologic Findings    Description: A. Sheets of plasma cells diffusely infiltrate the connective tissue with markedly attenuated surface epithelium (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×40). B. Bland plasmacytoid cells of uniform size intermingled with rare acute and chronic inflammatory cells (hematoxylin-eosin, original magnification ×400).
